decision_conditions: <span id="docs-internal-guid-20377c05-7fff-2a0b-76b3-478d05bb68a8"><div style="text-align: left;"><span id="docs-internal-guid-991c3a43-7fff-e775-4d3b-9a03fb59a6d6"><div style="text-align: justify; ">The proposal would use some poor quality external materials, the architectural and material choices would make the top storey appear excessively prominent in the townscape, the low level of glazing lacks animation, the north and east elevations would appear excessively blank and the proposed ground floor garden would create safety and security issues for its users. The proposal therefore creates unacceptable urban design impacts. This is contrary to Local Plan policy LP1 which requires all new development must be of the highest architectural and urban design quality, and London Plan policy D3 which requires all development to follow a design-led approach. Specifically the proposed development fails to adequately respond to the established local character and would neither be complementary nor compatible with the existing townscape.</div><div style="text-align: justify; "><br></div></span></div></span>

<div style="text-align: justify;">The submitted trip generation assessment appears to contain some data inconsistencies between the summary tables and raw TRICS database outputs. As such, insufficient details have been submitted to demonstrate that the proposal would not create unacceptable impacts on the capacity and safety of the highway network. This is contrary to Local Plan policies LP41 and LP43 and London Plan policies T1, T2, T4 and T7.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify;">It is unclear how all three proposed land uses would use a single bin store in the self-storage facility. Also, the scheme would require bins to be presented on the public footway for collection crews which would impede pedestrians. For these reasons the proposal has unacceptable waste &amp; recycling arrangements, contrary to Local Plan policy LP57.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify;">Minimum bat emergence survey visits have not been finalised. Insufficient details have been submitted in regard to the intended access, ongoing maintenance, and security management of the proposed garden.&nbsp; Insufficient justification has been submitted as to why integrated public realm landscaping could not be delivered along Matthias Road. Insufficient justification has been submitted as to why greening could not be integrated into the blank proposed north elevation to provide improved views for the school. The submission has therefore failed to demonstrate that it would have unacceptable biodiversity and impacts. This is contrary to Local Plan policies PP1, LP1, LP41, LP49, LP51 and LP54 which requires integrated landscaping/planting to enhance biodiversity, maximise greening opportunities and contribute to a healthier environment; and London Plan policies G6 and G7 which promote proposals that reduce deficiencies in access to nature.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify;">The proposal is for the demolition of the above ground elements of an existing building and construction of a new building. The area of the proposed garden provides an insufficiently small area of open space for the quantum of uses proposed. There would be no direct access from the proposed building to the garden. Also, the submission contains no detail as to when/if the single gated access into the garden would be locked so it is unclear whether it would be publicly accessible and usable where possible. This is contrary to Local Plan policy LP48 which requires all major commercial development to maximise on-site open space provision.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify;">There is insufficient justification in regard to: the difference in U-values between the unheated and heated spaces; mitigation of summer solar gain to the self-storage; sufficient space heating in colder months to the self-storage; water supply to the ‘Fab labs’; discrepancies between the Seasonal Coefficient of Performance (SCOP) of different uses; Energy Use Intensity (EUI) and Specific Heat Demand (SHD) of different spaces; active cooling being residual and mitigated as far as practicable through passive measures; reuse of existing assets being maximised; and why rainwater collection/harvesting is not being pursued. The submission has therefore failed to demonstrate acceptable sustainability and climate change&nbsp; impacts. This is contrary to Local Plan policy LP54 and London Plan policy SI 4 which require all new development to prioritise the regulation of internal and external temperatures through orientation, design, materials and technologies which avoid overheating, mitigate the Urban Heat Island effect and have regard to maximising the use of the cooling hierarchy.</div>

<div style="text-align: justify;">The proposed garden would lack passive surveillance. It is also unclear as to when/if the singular gated entrance to this space would be locked. Therefore, it would likely function as an unsafe space for its users and attract anti-social behaviour. The submitted drawings also contain insufficient detail of the proposed boundary treatment between the garden and the proposed yard to the west. As such, it is not clear if the yard would be sufficiently secure from intruders from the public garden. For these reasons, it has not been demonstrated that the proposal would be acceptable in safety and security terms. This is contrary to Local Plan policies PP1 and LP1 and London Plan policy D11.</div><div><br></div>

<p style="text-align: justify; ">The application contains insufficient SuDs details. Therefore, insufficient information has been submitted to demonstrate that the proposal would have acceptable flood risk and drainage impacts. This is contrary to Local Plan policy LP53 which requires all development must have regard to reducing flood risk, both to, and from the site, over its expected lifetime; and London Plan policy&nbsp; SI 13 which requires Lead Local Flood Authorities to identify and address increases in surface water run-off.</p><div style="text-align: justify; "><br></div>
description: Proposed and retrospective demolition of the above ground parts of an existing building; and erection of a part 3 and part 5-storey building containing self-storage floorspace (B8 use class), 8 flexible workspace / incubator units (E(c)(iii) / E(g)(ii) / E(g)(iii) use class) and 2 retail units (E(a) use class).
